functions.name: wizard1.lua
functions.sourceReview: Read the complete upstream dat/wizard1.lua program (lines 1-102). The loader preserves mazegrid initialization, mazelevel/noteleport/hardfloor flags, the pre-map bounds selection, centered 29-by-13 map placement with every transparent x cell, all level and teleport regions, the morgue room callback and its math.random wall choice, arrival room, mazewalk, ladder, four non-diggable and four non-passwall selections, fixed and class-random monster descriptors, the Wizard and Book of the Dead, board and random traps, random loot, and the final protected-selection hell_tweaks call in source order. Selection coordinate conversion and hell_tweaks follow the existing selvar.lua and nhlib.lua ports. No unported callee, obsolete guard, injected substitute, or swallowed refusal remains in this Lua program.

callers.source: The special-level registry dynamically imports wizard1_levels.js and spreads WIZARD1_LEVEL_LOADERS into SPECIAL_LEVEL_LOADERS, making the Lua program available under the wizard1 proto name.
sp_lev.c load_special() resolves SPECIAL_LEVEL_LOADERS[name], creates the special-level descriptor API, invokes the wizard1 loader, and runs finish() post-processing.
mkmaze.c makemaz() resolves the wizard1 special-level proto during makelevel() when Is_special() selects Wizard1's level, then dispatches it through load_special().

entryPointReview: The selected whole Lua program has one entry point: mkmaze.c makemaz() selects the wizard1 proto, load_special() dispatches the registered loader, and the descriptor API executes the complete dat/wizard1.lua program. The independent wizard-mode teleport recipe reaches this dispatch and records the resulting map, regions, walls, monsters, traps, objects, stairs, and hell_tweaks generation trace.
